papers.title: EEG-Based Cognitive Overload-Driven Adaptive Training for Enhancing Performance Under Simulated High-Stress Space Operation Tasks.
papers.summary: Proposes an EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training method combining hybrid feature selection, NFDTW-based feature alignment, and a shared knowledge layer, with a dual-factor task regulation strategy adjusting difficulty by performance and overload state. Achieved online overload detection accuracies of 92.07% and 84.67% on two datasets (up to 8.34% relative improvement) and, in a VR robotic arm docking task, the adaptive group showed significant gains in task performance and SAS versus fixed and control groups.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband, the study collected 180 multi-night recordings (23 participants) in SYNGAP1-related disorder and found interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants without electrographic seizures, plus increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered N1/N2/N3 staging, and elevated broadband power with reduced relative alpha power and alpha-theta ratio; spectral differences were tightly sleep-stage dependent.

papers.title: Same pipelines, different answers: how evaluation design shapes EEG seizure prediction
papers.summary: Holding five published seizure-prediction pipelines fixed and varying only the evaluation design on CHB-MIT, the authors found that subject-held-out partitions yielded near-chance AUCs (0.527–0.553) and that within-patient PSD+LDA dropped from AUC 0.815 with random window allocation to 0.572 with intact preictal blocks, with an index-based split leaking raw samples in all ten eligible cases. They release window manifests, partitions, and predictions for benchmarking.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: The authors built the Pediatric Cardiac Post-surgical Sleep (PCPS) expert-annotated polysomnography dataset and PCPS-SleepNet, a multi-band single-lead EEG deep learning framework with a Four-Stage Progressive Encoder and Conformer refinement, pre-trained on public data and fine-tuned on PCPS. Subject-independent validation reached 75.65% accuracy and 89.06% AUROC for staging, and 87.89% AUPRC for slow wave sleep detection.

papers.title: Coordinated Drift of Image Representations in Human EEG
papers.summary: Using the multi-session THINGS-EEG2 dataset, the authors showed that image-evoked EEG response patterns drift across recording sessions in a coordinated, channel-wide manner concentrated along image-identity dimensions, impairing average cross-session decoding while preserving global distance statistics and response-space dimensionality. Simulations indicate Hebbian downstream networks adapt faster to such structured drift than to unstructured drift.

papers.title: Quantifying Interictal Spike Asymmetry on Scalp EEG to Lateralize the Seizure-Onset Zone in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study (365 drug-resistant TLE patients) quantifying automatically detected interictal spike rate asymmetry on scalp EEG with a deep learning model and leave-one-hemisphere-out lateralization to predict clinician-annotated seizure focus. Left-vs-right/bilateral classification reached AUC 0.78 (70% accuracy) and right-vs-left/bilateral AUC 0.80 (75% accuracy); model-surgery concordance was associated with favorable Engel I outcomes.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine disrupts sleep architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's disease model and wild-type mice.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
papers.summary: Chronic oral diphenhydramine (10 mg/kg, one month) was tested in female 5XFAD and wild-type mice with wireless EEG/EMG telemetry; at baseline 5XFAD mice spent more time in NREM1 and had shorter REM and NREM2 bouts, and diphenhydramine fragmented NREM2 in both genotypes, increased NREM1 and REM during the active phase, and disrupted light-dark sleep distribution without rescuing 5XFAD deficits.

papers.title: Style transfer mapping with ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a Prototype-Consistent Style Transfer Mapping framework with confidence-aware transductive semi-supervised adaptation and reliability-aware ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition, reporting stable performance under a leave-one-pair-out protocol on public EEG datasets of major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: A representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework for spectral analysis and detection of epileptiform patterns in pediatric EEG: computational validation with a roadmap for external benchmarking.
papers.summary: The authors developed a representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework with adaptive denoising, energy-criterion EMD, weighted time-frequency fusion, eight spectral-temporal features, and a soft-voting SVM/random forest/neural network ensemble, achieving 94.6% accuracy and AUROC 0.971 on 2,000 synthetic pediatric EEG segments and AUROC 0.901 on CHB-MIT leave-one-subject-out feasibility validation.

papers.title: A generative framework for estimating brain energy landscapes from continuous neuroimaging observations.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a hierarchical generative pairwise maximum entropy model linking latent binary brain states to continuous observations, with node-specific baseline/gain parameters, compound-symmetry noise, and an EEG/MEG leadfield forward model instead of an inverse-first reconstruction. Simulations showed improved recovery of fields, couplings, and latent states, and application to propofol sedation EEG revealed pipeline-dependent condition effects in residual spatial correlation and basin entropy not seen with conventional demean-based pMEM.

papers.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
papers.summary: Develops a two-stage data-driven variational Galerkin framework that first learns the fixed-lag Kolmogorov backward operator (e.g., via Fourier Neural Operator) and then compresses it onto a finite-dimensional observable space for spectral analysis and forecasting, with error analysis tracing learning, sampling, and invariance/reconstruction errors to spectra and forecasts. Numerical experiments illustrate spectral approximation, long-rollout stability, and comparison with extended dynamic mode decomposition under limited transition data.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography
papers.summary: Developed and validated WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of spreading depolarizations based on delta-band spatiotemporal propagation, trained against invasive subdural ECoG in 32 patients with TBI, SAH, or malignant hemispheric stroke (1,119 annotated SDs). WAVEFRONT achieved a cross-validated true positive rate of 97.3±1% at 6.0±0.5% false positive rate, and in an external cardiac-arrest cohort (I-CARE) showed greater SD burden on day 3 in patients with poor versus good neurological outcome (p=0.007).

papers.title: Towards improving Alzheimer's intervention: a machine learning approach for biomarker detection through combining MEG and MRI pipelines.
papers.summary: Evaluates MEG-derived spectral biomarkers at sensor and source levels (five inverse solutions including LCMV and eLORETA) with MRI anatomical features to classify 166 healthy controls versus 158 MCI participants in the BioFIND cohort using nested cross-validation with Monte Carlo replication. Best performance came from combining source-based MEG with MRI features using GLMNET, reaching 76.31±1.47% accuracy and 82.44±1.44% AUC, with MEG-only models outperforming MRI-only analyses.

papers.title: GeoMind: Dancing with Geometric Brain Rhythm on Symmetric Positive Definite Manifolds.
papers.summary: Proposed GeoMind, a geometric state space model neural network that tracks evolving brain states as trajectories on a Riemannian manifold of symmetric positive definite functional connectivity matrices. Reported promising brain-state identification on task fMRI and early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and autism from resting-state fMRI, and outperformed competing methods on EEG emotion datasets.

papers.title: Robust Epilepsy Diagnosis in Neonates Via Spatio-Temporal Graph Learning and Balanced Test-Time Training.
papers.summary: Presented a cross-subject deep learning framework for neonatal epilepsy diagnosis from EEG that models multichannel signals as spatio-temporal graphs with balanced test-time training for domain adaptation. On 140 neonates (70 healthy, 70 epileptic) it achieved segment-level accuracy of 83% and AUC 0.90, with subject-level accuracy rising from 0.79 to 0.88 with balanced test-time training.

papers.title: Beyond Static Representations: Learning Electroencephalogram Spatiotemporal Dynamics for Enhanced Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed DSE-TAM, a framework combining dynamic spatial embedding via graph convolutional networks with a Temporal Attention Mamba module integrating self-attention and state-space models for EEG emotion recognition. Reported accuracies of 79.75%/78.27% (arousal/valence) on DEAP, 80.55%/83.91% on DREAMER, and 73.75% (3-class) on an in-house CEED dataset, surpassing state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Replacing EEG with peripheral physiological signals for driving behavior recognition: a physiology-informed multimodal approach.
papers.summary: Tested whether low-cost peripheral physiological signals (ECG, EMG, GSR) can replace EEG for driving behavior recognition using a physiology-informed multimodal learning framework on a simulator dataset of 35 participants across five driving behaviors. The ECG+EMG+GSR configuration achieved 0.795 accuracy and 0.805 macro-F1 under five-fold cross-validation, outperforming the EEG-only setting and six baseline methods.

papers.title: Auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness and propofol-based anesthesia
papers.summary: Used stereoelectroencephalography in 13 epilepsy patients to jointly characterize auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness versus propofol-based anesthesia. Anesthesia reduced stimulus-rate power and phase alignment, weakened the distance-response relationship from Heschl's gyrus, and lowered acoustic-envelope decoding accuracy in contrastive learning (CEBRA) embeddings.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG functional connectivity changes following memantine administration in children with autism spectrum disorder: an exploratory pre-post study.
papers.summary: Exploratory pre-post study assessing resting-state EEG functional connectivity (Phase Locking Value, graph theory, spatial pattern of network analysis) before and after one month of memantine in 22 preschool children with autism spectrum disorder. Found heterogeneous reorganization: 64% showed increased network integration and 36% decreased connectivity, with localized fronto-central/left occipital decoupling alongside enhanced long-range coupling and nodal centrality in right parietal and left temporal regions.

papers.title: E-MDD: an evidence-guided explainable framework for EEG-based depression recognition.
papers.summary: Developed E-MDD, a three-stage framework fusing EEG latent features with neurophysiological biomarkers and using a large language model to generate evidence-guided textual explanations for depression recognition, achieving AUC 0.8472 and F1-score 0.8421 on the Mumtaz dataset with faithful explanations replicated across EEGNet and EEGConformer.

papers.title: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: In persons with Parkinson's disease, EEG analysis showed that levodopa administration and subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation altered β-band event-locked responses, event-related potentials, δ-band neural tracking of isochronous auditory rhythm, and excitation/inhibition balance; changes in E/I were linked to UPDRS-III motor severity under levodopa.

papers.title: EEG-based brain effective and functional connectivity predict PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: Resting-state dry EEG effective and functional connectivity features trained machine learning models predicting PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals with accuracy comparable to or exceeding plasma p-tau217 and other predictors, and identified brain regions and connections associated with neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Federated Spiking GANs with Rényi Differential Privacy for privacy-preserving synthetic EEG generation in brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: The authors developed a federated spiking GAN framework combining an SNN-based generator, temporally correlated noise, an ANN discriminator, and Rényi differential privacy to generate synthetic EEG data; it preserved temporal features and downstream utility while maintaining privacy relative to RDP-TimeGAN, RDP-CRNN-GAN, RDP-RCGAN, and RDP-Clare-GAN comparators.

papers.title: Motor cortex-based intracortical BCI performance is robust to changes in attentional load during dual-tasking.
papers.summary: Examined the effect of increased attentional load (via a concurrent N-Back task) on intracortical BCI cursor control in two participants with tetraplegia, finding iBCI performance was largely robust to dual-tasking despite EEG theta/alpha increases suggesting higher attentional load, with one participant showing a small delay in the mild-load condition.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG was compared between 74 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls, analyzing spectral power and functional connectivity across multiple bands. No EEG contrast survived correction for multiple comparisons, indicating that large or widespread alterations were not detectable; occipital/global alpha power and temporal theta showed only nominal differences.

papers.title: Naturalistic language assessment and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia for precision neurorehabilitation.
papers.summary: Integrative review synthesizing evidence on naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging (EEG/fNIRS), and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia, proposing an operational ecological biomarker framework linking connected-speech features, neural measures, and longitudinal outcomes for precision neurorehabilitation.

papers.title: EEG decodability of facial expressions and their stereoscopic depth cues in immersive virtual reality
papers.summary: Combined immersive VR, EEG, and eye tracking in 34 participants to show that time-resolved multivariate decoding reliably differentiates facial expressions and detects a distinct neural signature of stereoscopic depth cues, while expression decoding remained invariant across depth conditions.

papers.title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed a two-stage layer-adaptive framework built on EEG Conformer that uses differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers to locate and suppress subject-specific interference, plus a subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer, improving cross-subject EEG emotion recognition under leave-one-subject-out evaluation on SEED and SEED-IV.

papers.title: Improvement in naming with tDCS and alteration of functional connectivity in post-stroke aphasia: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a double-blind sham-controlled randomized trial of 60 post-stroke aphasia patients, anodal tDCS over the left Sylvian parietal temporal region plus speech-language therapy for four weeks produced significantly greater improvements in picture naming and auditory word-picture identification than sham (p < 0.001). EEG cross-approximate entropy showed increased functional connectivity across multiple left-hemisphere and bilateral temporal electrode pairs after tDCS.

papers.title: Assessment of the duration of continuous EEG monitoring in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
papers.summary: In a retrospective comparison of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients receiving standard 6–7-day versus longer (>7-day) continuous EEG monitoring, longer monitoring was associated with nearly doubled ICU and hospital length of stay but not with vasospasm, delayed cerebral ischemia, or 6-month functional outcome.

papers.title: Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 300 mechanically ventilated ICU patients with continuous video-EEG, burst suppression duration was an independent delirium risk factor and predicted delirium with an AUC of 0.871 (cutoff 41.5 s: 80.8% sensitivity, 78.2% specificity); combining burst suppression duration with bispectral index raised the AUC to 0.914.

papers.title: AAV-mediated Modulation of Dorsal Raphe Serotonergic Neurons Recapitulates Fenfluramine Efficacy in a Rat Model of Dravet Syndrome.
papers.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
papers.summary: In a Scn1a+/- rat model of Dravet syndrome, chronic fenfluramine reduced hyperthermia-induced seizure frequency, attenuated EEG network hypersynchrony, and ameliorated hyperactivity and depressive-like comorbidities alongside reduced hippocampal neuroinflammation. AAV-mediated modulation of dorsal raphe serotonergic neurons was sufficient to reproduce the key antiseizure and electrophysiological effects of fenfluramine.

papers.title: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
papers.summary: Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict while receiving tactile feedback with or without explicit spatial landmarks. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness and were associated with increased somatosensory activity and more restricted sensorimotor connectivity, whereas non-spatial touch was linked to widespread cortical reductions and diffuse connectivity.

papers.title: General information reliability, perceived educational quality, and transparency of YouTube videos on epileptiform discharges: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study rated 25 English-language YouTube videos on epileptiform discharges using DISCERN, the Global Quality Scale, and JAMA criteria, finding moderate-to-good average perceived educational quality and information reliability but limited transparency (mean JAMA 1.98). The authors emphasize that the instruments are not EEG-specific and the findings are exploratory, without assessment of EEG accuracy or learner outcomes.

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapped 60 EEG studies of cognitive functioning in people with cancer, finding that task-based event-related potentials (especially oddball and attention tasks) predominated over quantitative EEG, with longer P300 latency and lower amplitude common in non-CNS cancers but inconsistent and often untested associations with cognitive outcomes. The authors conclude the evidence is methodologically heterogeneous and call for larger longitudinal studies with consistent cognitive measures.

papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβ γ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response
papers.summary: Integrated human genetic analysis with cellular assays to classify GNAO1 variants into those that sequester Gβγ versus those reducing Go expression, showing that impaired Gβγ release is associated with the hyperkinetic NEDIM phenotype. In GNAO1R209H/+ mice, caffeine and gallein both reduced hyperlocomotion, and patch-clamp recordings revealed sex- and cell-type-specific hyperexcitability in dorsolateral striatal spiny projection neurons.

papers.title: Machine learning based on behavioral, fecal and oocyst analyses for chicken coccidiosis diagnosis: A systematic review with exploratory extension.
papers.summary: This systematic review with exploratory extension summarizes machine learning applications for chicken coccidiosis diagnosis across behavioral physiology, fecal characteristics, and oocyst morphology, noting that fecal- and oocyst-image recognition alone struggles with early screening and generalization under field conditions. It proposes a conceptual multimodal AI surveillance framework integrating behavioral screening, fecal validation, and oocyst species identification, counting, sporulation-state classification, and viability assessment.

papers.title: Assessment of Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence Guidance in the Management of Patients Referred Following a First Suspected Seizure: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
papers.summary: Retrospective clinical audit of 53 patients referred to a first-seizure clinic, assessing adherence to NICE guidance on specialist assessment, ECG, EEG, neuroimaging, recurrence-risk assessment, and safety advice. Compliance was high for ECG (100%), recurrence-risk documentation (100%), and safety-netting/driving advice (100%), but only 9.4% had specialist assessment within two weeks and EEG was markedly delayed (mean ~12.5 weeks), identifying timely EEG access as the largest gap.

papers.title: Three repeated intrathecal injections of allogenic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells in autism spectrum disorder: a Phase I clinical trial.
papers.summary: Phase I open-label trial testing three repeated intrathecal injections of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (20×10⁶ per dose at one-month intervals) in five children with autism spectrum disorder. Treatment was safe and well-tolerated with no serious adverse events; exploratory behavioral improvements on CARS were seen in all children and CSF TNF-α and IL-6 levels consistently decreased, supporting immunomodulatory effects and warranting larger controlled trials.

papers.title: Electrophysiology Team-Administered Conscious Sedation for Pulsed-Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: Randomized 1:1 trial in 120 patients with symptomatic drug-refractory atrial fibrillation comparing electrophysiology team-administered conscious sedation for pulsed-field ablation versus radiofrequency ablation, assessing tolerance, procedural efficiency, and safety. PFA showed lower FPS-R pain scores and shorter total procedure and left atrial dwell times, with higher cough incidence during pulmonary vein isolation (21.7% vs 6.7%) but no serious sedation-related complications, supporting feasibility of EP team-administered conscious sedation for PFA in selected low-risk patients.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
